subproblem.title: Good slicing radii in the dyadic intervals ((1/2)^{j+3}, (1/2)^{j+2})
subproblem.statement: Assume, as a hypothesis of the statement, (GR), the frozen type of Submission.cmcsd_good_radius: for P ∈ ℕ, finite measures μ, μ′ on ℝ^P (IsFiniteMeasure), f : ℝ^P → ℝ measurable, a real ρ > 0 and B ∈ [0, ∞] with μ({f < ρ}) ≤ B, there is r with ρ/2 < r < ρ, liminf_{h→0+} ofReal(h⁻¹)·μ({r − h < f < r}) ≤ ofReal(4/ρ)·B and liminf_{h→0+} ofReal(h⁻¹)·μ′({r − h < f < r}) < ∞ (liminf along the filter 𝓝[>] 0, values in [0, ∞]). Let P, m ∈ ℕ, let μ, μ′ be finite measures on ℝ^P, d : ℝ^P → ℝ measurable, C ∈ ℝ≥0 and M, M′ ∈ [0, ∞] with M ≠ ∞ and M′ ≠ ∞, and assume that for every real r with 0 < r ≤ 1/4, μ({d < r}) ≤ C·ofReal(r^{m+2})·M and μ′({d < r}) ≤ C·ofReal(r^{m+2})·M′ (in [0, ∞], ofReal = ENNReal.ofReal). Then there is r : ℕ → ℝ such that: (i) (1/2)^{j+3} < r_j < (1/2)^{j+2} for every j ∈ ℕ; (ii) r is strictly decreasing; (iii) for every j, μ({d < r_j}) ≤ C·ofReal((1/2)^{(j+2)(m+2)})·M and μ′({d < r_j}) ≤ C·ofReal((1/2)^{(j+2)(m+2)})·M′; (iv) μ({d < r_j}) → 0 and μ′({d < r_j}) → 0 as j → ∞; (v) for every j, liminf_{h→0+} ofReal(h⁻¹)·μ({r_j − h < d < r_j}) ≤ 4·C·ofReal((1/2)^{(j+2)(m+1)})·M; (vi) for every j, liminf_{h→0+} ofReal(h⁻¹)·μ′({r_j − h < d < r_j}) < ∞. Here liminf is taken along the filter 𝓝[>] 0 of right neighbourhoods of 0, and {r_j − h < d < r_j} = {x : r_j − h < d(x) ∧ d(x) < r_j}.
subproblem.lean_statement: (∀ (P : ℕ) (μ μ' : Measure (Euclid P)) (f : Euclid P → ℝ) (ρ : ℝ) (B : ℝ≥0∞), IsFiniteMeasure μ → IsFiniteMeasure μ' → Measurable f → 0 < ρ → μ {x | f x < ρ} ≤ B → ∃ r ∈ Ioo (ρ / 2) ρ, liminf (fun h : ℝ => ENNReal.ofReal h⁻¹ * μ {x | r - h < f x ∧ f x < r}) (𝓝[>] 0) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (4 / ρ) * B ∧ liminf (fun h : ℝ => ENNReal.ofReal h⁻¹ * μ' {x | r - h < f x ∧ f x < r}) (𝓝[>] 0) < ∞) → ∀ (P m : ℕ) (μ μ' : Measure (Euclid P)) (d : Euclid P → ℝ) (C : NNReal) (M M' : ℝ≥0∞), IsFiniteMeasure μ → IsFiniteMeasure μ' → Measurable d → M ≠ ∞ → M' ≠ ∞ → (∀ r : ℝ, 0 < r → r ≤ 1 / 4 → μ {x | d x < r} ≤ C * ENNReal.ofReal (r ^ (m + 2)) * M ∧ μ' {x | d x < r} ≤ C * ENNReal.ofReal (r ^ (m + 2)) * M') → ∃ r : ℕ → ℝ, (∀ j, (1 / 2 : ℝ) ^ (j + 3) < r j ∧ r j < (1 / 2 : ℝ) ^ (j + 2)) ∧ StrictAnti r ∧ (∀ j, μ {x | d x < r j} ≤ C * ENNReal.ofReal ((1 / 2 : ℝ) ^ ((j + 2) * (m + 2))) * M ∧ μ' {x | d x < r j} ≤ C * ENNReal.ofReal ((1 / 2 : ℝ) ^ ((j + 2) * (m + 2))) * M') ∧ Tendsto (fun j => μ {x | d x < r j}) atTop (𝓝 0) ∧ Tendsto (fun j => μ' {x | d x < r j}) atTop (𝓝 0) ∧ (∀ j, liminf (fun h : ℝ => ENNReal.ofReal h⁻¹ * μ {x | r j - h < d x ∧ d x < r j}) (𝓝[>] 0) ≤ 4 * C * ENNReal.ofReal ((1 / 2 : ℝ) ^ ((j + 2) * (m + 1))) * M) ∧ (∀ j, liminf (fun h : ℝ => ENNReal.ofReal h⁻¹ * μ' {x | r j - h < d x ∧ d x < r j}) (𝓝[>] 0) < ∞)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 5 of the parent-supplied proof of cmcsd_shell_decomposition, with the density estimates of its steps 11(b) and 13(iii); Simon, Introduction to GMT, Ch. 6, proof of the deformation theorem 5.1, displays (8)–(10) (book/chapter-06.txt lines 1405–1928) (display (10): ρ ∈ (σ/2, σ) with M⟨T, d, ρ⟩ ≤ (c/σ)·M(T_σ − T_{σ/2})).
1. Put ρ_j := (1/2)^{j+2}. Then ρ_j > 0, ρ_j ≤ (1/2)^2 = 1/4 (pow_le_pow_of_le_one, since j + 2 ≥ 2) and ρ_j/2 = (1/2)^{j+3} (pow_succ).
2. (Choice of r_j; (i) and (vi).) Fix j and put B_j := C·ofReal(ρ_j^{m+2})·M. By the hypothesis with r := ρ_j, μ({d < ρ_j}) ≤ B_j. GR, applied with μ, μ′ (finite), f := d (measurable), ρ := ρ_j > 0 and B := B_j, gives r_j with ρ_j/2 < r_j < ρ_j, liminf_{h→0+} ofReal(h⁻¹)·μ({r_j − h < d < r_j}) ≤ ofReal(4/ρ_j)·B_j and liminf_{h→0+} ofReal(h⁻¹)·μ′({r_j − h < d < r_j}) < ∞. Choose such an r_j for every j (axiom of choice). By step 1 this gives (i), and (vi) holds.
3. ((ii).) For every j, r_{j+1} < (1/2)^{j+3} < r_j by (i) (applied to j + 1 and to j). Hence r is strictly decreasing (strictAnti_nat_of_succ_lt).
4. ((iii).) Since r_j < ρ_j, {d < r_j} ⊆ {d < ρ_j}, so μ({d < r_j}) ≤ μ({d < ρ_j}) ≤ C·ofReal(ρ_j^{m+2})·M by the hypothesis with r := ρ_j, and ρ_j^{m+2} = ((1/2)^{j+2})^{m+2} = (1/2)^{(j+2)(m+2)} (pow_mul). The same argument with μ′ and M′ gives the second inequality.
5. ((iv).) Since (j + 2)(m + 2) ≥ j → ∞ and (1/2)^n → 0 (tendsto_pow_atTop_nhds_zero_of_lt_one), (1/2)^{(j+2)(m+2)} → 0, hence ofReal((1/2)^{(j+2)(m+2)}) → ofReal 0 = 0 (ENNReal.tendsto_ofReal). As C ≠ ∞ and M ≠ ∞, C·ofReal((1/2)^{(j+2)(m+2)})·M → C·0·M = 0 (ENNReal.Tendsto.const_mul, ENNReal.Tendsto.mul_const). By (iii), 0 ≤ μ({d < r_j}) ≤ C·ofReal((1/2)^{(j+2)(m+2)})·M, so μ({d < r_j}) → 0 (tendsto_of_tendsto_of_tendsto_of_le_of_le). The same argument with μ′ and M′ ≠ ∞ gives μ′({d < r_j}) → 0.
6. ((v).) For ρ > 0 we have (4/ρ)·ρ^{m+2} = 4ρ^{m+1}, hence ofReal(4/ρ)·ofReal(ρ^{m+2}) = ofReal(4ρ^{m+1}) = 4·ofReal(ρ^{m+1}) (ENNReal.ofReal_mul with 4/ρ ≥ 0 and with 4 ≥ 0; ENNReal.ofReal_ofNat). Using commutativity and associativity of multiplication in [0, ∞], ofReal(4/ρ_j)·B_j = C·(ofReal(4/ρ_j)·ofReal(ρ_j^{m+2}))·M = 4·C·ofReal(ρ_j^{m+1})·M, and ρ_j^{m+1} = (1/2)^{(j+2)(m+1)} (pow_mul). With the liminf bound of step 2 this gives (v). ∎
proof_key_steps: GR with B_j = C·ofReal(ρ_j^{m+2})·M (density hypothesis at ρ_j) gives r_j ∈ (ρ_j/2, ρ_j) with both liminf bounds; choose for all j.
r_{j+1} < (1/2)^{j+3} < r_j, so r is strictly decreasing.
μ({d < r_j}) ≤ μ({d < ρ_j}) ≤ C·ofReal((1/2)^{(j+2)(m+2)})·M (pow_mul), and the same for μ′; this bound tends to 0.
ofReal(4/ρ)·ofReal(ρ^{m+2}) = 4·ofReal(ρ^{m+1}) turns the GR bound into 4·C·ofReal((1/2)^{(j+2)(m+1)})·M.

audit.reason: GR is applied with exactly its stated hypotheses at positive radii at most 1/4. The chosen intervals imply strict decrease, measure monotonicity gives both density bounds, finite M and M′ justify convergence to zero, and the positive-radius algebra gives the exact factor 4 and exponent m+1.
